title: The Celebrity Club in Harlem and its first European-bound records
summary: The 125th Street club drew a mixed crowd and Europeans; first records were for Larry Newton at Derby, with five or six tours.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: The Celebrity Club's on 105th -- 125th between 5th and Madison. It's right off of Madison. It's between 5th and Madison. It was nice then. It was really nice. Everybody was coming uptown, white and black, you know, everybody. So then, you know, like we put the thing on the map because everytime European people would come, they'd come straight to the Celebrity Club because then we started record-
We recorded -- first record was for Larry Newton. He was the President of Derby. He later went over to ABC. You might know the name, Larry Newton. I think ABC -- was ABC Paramount?

Yeah, I think he went over there. And I don't know where Larry is now. Then he had quite a bit of distribution in Europe and Panacsee did a lot of things, you know, he thought I was just his man, you know, and everything. He really made me in Europe, you know, from the Hot Club in France, you know, and played my records all the time and everything. He just did everything, you know.

So then we started being asked to bring the band to Europe. We made about five trips, five or six trips with the Celebrity Club band to Europe. So then we were playing like all the club dances. See, what we were doing, Gary, we were playing for -- this club was like people would rent the hall and we went with the hall at Celebrity Club and we furnished the music, but the man paid us. But then, we started getting dances like our other places, clubs, you know, want us to play the -- we played all over New York. You know, like sometime they would rent the Hotel Diplomat and they'd rent all the big -- sometime the -- we played the Commodore.
Then I'd have to augment the band sometime because the minimum may be ten, may be eleven.
